concepts.title: The Conquest as Negotiated Process
concepts.excerpt: What appears in European histories as Spanish conquest — military triumph through superior technology and indigenous demoralization — inverts completely when read through indigenous sources.

concepts.title: Marina (Malinche): Translator as Indispensable Agent
concepts.excerpt: Marina appears in Spanish historical accounts as traitor — the indigenous woman who abandoned her people to serve Spanish invaders.

concepts.title: Smallpox as Force Multiplier, Not Determinant
concepts.excerpt: Smallpox killed without regard for Spanish authority or indigenous resistance.

concepts.title: Moctezuma's Pragmatism: Rational Strategy vs. Fatalism Narrative
concepts.excerpt: European historical narratives portray Moctezuma II as paralyzed by fatalism — believing Cortés was the god Quetzalcoatl returning, unable to act decisively, surrendering through mystical resignation rather than rational calculation.

concepts.title: Altepetl: Indigenous Political Units in Pre-Columbian and Colonial Governance
concepts.excerpt: The altepetl (literally "water-mountain," used to mean city-state or polity) was the fundamental political unit of Nahua civilization.

concepts.title: Calpolli: Decentralized Administration Through Kinship Structure
concepts.excerpt: The calpolli (neighborhood or kin-group) was the fundamental administrative unit within each altepetl.

concepts.title: Tlatoani: Paramount Chief as Negotiator Under Constraint
concepts.excerpt: The tlatoani (paramount chief, literally "he who speaks") was not autocrat with absolute power.

concepts.title: Xiuhpohualli: The 52-Year Calendar System
concepts.excerpt: The xiuhpohualli (52-year cycle calendar) structured how Nahua peoples understood time, history, and existence itself.

concepts.title: Chimalpahin's Annals: Indigenous Historiography as Archive and Assertion
concepts.excerpt: Chimalpahin (1579-1660) was indigenous historian who wrote annals of his altepetl (Amecameca) and the broader Nahua world using xiuhpohualli calendar framework in early 17th century.

concepts.title: Translator Invisibility: The Hidden Scaffolding of Historic Change
concepts.excerpt: Translation operates in historical narratives the way electrical wiring operates in buildings: foundational to what is visible and functional, but structurally invisible because attention is directed away from it toward the visible output.

concepts.title: Agency vs. Structure: How Individual Choices Navigate Institutional Inevitability
concepts.excerpt: The conquest of the Mexica appears in two irreconcilable narratives: one where Spanish military superiority made indigenous defeat inevitable (structure-as-destiny), and one where Marina's translation, Tlaxcaltec alliance decisions, and Moctezuma's pragmatism made victory contingent on specific human choices (agency-as-determinative).

concepts.title: Pragmatism vs. Ideology: How Practical Choices Get Reinterpreted as Inevitable Beliefs
concepts.excerpt: Moctezuma negotiates with Spanish instead of mobilizing total military resistance.

concepts.title: Atheism as State Violence: Religious Suppression as Governance Mechanism
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a person who finds meaning through prayer, community, ritual, and the belief in something transcendent.

concepts.title: Machiavellian Glory Hierarchy
concepts.excerpt: Before giving tactical advice, Machiavelli states what he thinks worthy objectives look like.

concepts.title: Coxinga Rebellion: When Two Powers Claim the Same Throne
concepts.excerpt: Imagine two chess players where both have genuinely superior positions, but neither can prove it without destroying the logic the game is built on.

concepts.title: Manchu Conquest of 1644: Information Dominance as Strategic Weapon
concepts.excerpt: Picture a fortress that falls not because its walls are breached but because the defenders have misunderstood what siege they are under.

concepts.title: Archive as Resistance: Documentation as Political Act Under Colonialism
concepts.excerpt: The archive is not neutral preservation of facts. It is a political choice — what to record, how to frame it, what language to write in, whose perspective matters.

concepts.title: The Untold Story Problem: How Narrative Frame Determines What Counts as Strength and Weakness
concepts.excerpt: Flower wars are perfect illustration of untold story problem: indigenous ritual conflict appears as military genius from indigenous frame (sophisticated statecraft system that maintains alliance, generates sacrifice victims, demonstrates power without destructive total war).

concepts.title: Identity Maintenance Under Threat: Preserving Essential Self When External Structure Collapses
concepts.excerpt: Identity is not purely internal psychological fact.

concepts.title: Language Death as Bioultural Collapse
concepts.excerpt: This concept cannot be understood without simultaneously holding linguistic and ecological/anthropological frames — when the last fluent speaker of a minority language dies, the 150 words for moorland-and-peat that the language carried die with them, and the ecological knowledge embedded in those words (where peat is dryable, which moorland is dangerous in fog, what soil supports what plant) dies too, because the knowledge is inalienable from the lexicon.
